beguile

/bih-GYLE/ - rhymes with mile · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Beguile means to deceive someone by means of charm.

The market vendor beguiled tourists into paying triple for ordinary prints, chatting so warmly that none of them thought to bargain.

Worked Example

The double agent beguiled the embassy staff for a decade: he hosted the best dinners in the quarter, told the funniest stories, and left each evening with one more careless remark filed away in his memory.

Beguile names deception that works through delight. Enchanting and charming someone can be perfectly innocent, and a cheat can rob you without ever being liked — but to beguile is to make the deceiving itself feel like pleasure, so the victim opens the door and smiles.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

enchant: To enchant is to delight and captivate — an enchanting host, an enchanting view — with no dishonesty implied anywhere. Beguile borrows that same delight and puts it to work as deception: the beguiled victim is being charmed precisely so they will not notice they are being robbed or misled.

sweet-talk: Sweet-talk is light, transparent coaxing — everyone can see the game, and the worst it costs is a favor granted with a knowing smile. Beguile is darker: it hides a genuine deception inside real charm, so the victim never sees the game until the damage is done.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

repel: drives people away instead of drawing them in

disillusion: breaks a pleasant spell instead of casting one

Where it sits · how deceptive the appeal becomes — please → charm → beguile

please vs. beguile: Please sits far below beguile on the ladder: pleasing someone wins a smile and nothing more, with no hold taken over anyone.

charm vs. beguile: Charm stops short of beguile: charm draws people to you and may be entirely honest, while beguile turns that same warmth into an instrument of deception.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — be-

Prefix — be-: thoroughly, all around

Root — guile

Root — guile: cunning deceit (Old French)

Put it together

Put it together: Be- is the old intensifying prefix that means 'thoroughly, all over' — the same be- as in bewilder — and guile is cunning deceit. To beguile someone is literally to wrap them all around in guile: deception applied so warmly and so completely that it feels like friendship.

Use the root on its own: guile

Use the root on its own: guile: Guile — a word you will study in this same unit — is the deceit itself: the outnumbered general's guile won battles that his soldiers never could have.

Word Choice

literary / warm-toned

Beguile is the storyteller's word for deception that feels delightful while it works. If the flattery is a means to a favor, blandish — also in this unit — is more exact; if you mean the cunning itself, that is guile. Beguile keeps the spotlight on the victim's enchantment.
